proposals.evidence: Full cōkṣa explicitly gives Gujarati cokhā rice, Sindhi cokho cleaned rice and Kachhi caukhā rice, alongside Prakrit cokkha/cukkha. These support the western cukhā/cukkā/cukā/tsoka/sukhā rice responses. The semantic development is documented rather than inferred only from clean. Source affricate/sibilant, aspiration, gemination, vowels and internal spacing remain intact; local phonetic history and cross-IA transmission are qualified. Exact response: tsu kha.

proposals.evidence: Full śāli explicitly gives Gujarati/Marathi sāḷ and regional sāl rice, with Sinhalese häl/äl also documented. These support western sāl/sāḷ and provisionally Noiri hal as a family member, retaining the uncertain local s-to-h history without claiming a Sinhalese loan. Source lateral quality and the broad rice gloss remain intact; unhusked/growing senses in the dictionary are not silently imposed on the source record. Cross-IA transmission is qualified. Exact response: sāl.
